name: Treaty with the Creeks, 1790 (Treaty of New York)
promises: Article 4: the boundary between the United States and the Creek Nation was fixed, the Creeks ceded the land north and east of it, and the United States would pay $1,500 a year and deliver goods.
Article 5: the United States solemnly guaranteed to the Creek Nation all their lands within the United States west and south of that boundary.
Article 6: a citizen who tried to settle on Creek lands would forfeit the protection of the United States, and the Creeks could punish him as they pleased.
Article 7: no citizen was to hunt on Creek lands or enter the Creek country without a passport.
today: In Docket 275 the Indian Claims Commission (1970) held that the Article 5 guarantee was an undertaking to protect the Creeks' aboriginal occupancy against Georgia and white settlers, not a grant of recognized title. No court or Commission finding that a promise of this treaty was broken was located.

openQuestions: The Article 5 guarantee covered Creek land later taken by the Treaty of Fort Jackson (1814), which was the subject of the Commission's Docket 21; that docket concerns the 1814 treaty, not this one, and was not read for this record.
The Muscogee (Creek) Nation's own account of the 1790 treaty was not located.
The secret articles of the treaty were not reviewed.
